dedupe_keys.name: cal itp and caltrans dds statewide california gtfs derived transit routes stops speeds and high quality transit areas

description: The California Integrated Travel Project (Cal-ITP) is a state programme that brings common standards for fares, eligibility checks and real-time information to California's hundreds of transit providers, and with Caltrans' Division of Data and Digital Services (DDS) it ingests every provider's GTFS feeds into statewide transit data products. Cal-ITP is funded through CalSTA and Caltrans by the Transit and Intercity Rail Capital Program; DDS analysts publish the analyses. Coverage: all public transit operators in California. Published layers include statewide transit routes and stops, average transit speeds by stop-to-stop segment and by route and time of day, high-quality transit areas and major bus stops under state planning law, GTFS digests by operator and legislative district, real-time performance metrics per operator and stop, and National Transit Database ridership summaries, with a data dictionary for the GTFS ingest pipeline. Format and access: ArcGIS feature and map services on the Caltrans GIS server, downloads on the California open data portal, dashboards in the analyses portfolio and source code on GitHub; free. Licence: California open data terms for the published layers (not read per layer); analysis code on GitHub. Caveats: layers inherit the quality of each operator's GTFS, and speeds from real-time feeds are missing for operators without vehicle positions. Simulation uses: statewide transit network topology and service levels for network flow, accessibility and capacity planning models, and bus stop exposure to hazards. Related records: the GTFS specification (data-gtfs-specification) defines the source feeds, and Caltrans PeMS (data-caltrans-pems) covers the state highway side.
